This strongly points to **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**. The symptom description explicitly states: "A white slimy bacterial substance streams from a freshly cut stem base placed in water, which is a strong indicator of bacteria in the vascular tissue."

Let me now view reference images across 4 different classes to satisfy the budget requirement.
Southern_Bacterial_Wilt reference shows brown pith discoloration inside a split stem — consistent with the test image's stem showing brown streaking. Now let me check other candidates.

This Bacterial_Wilt reference (Bugwood ID 5606063) is essentially the same streaming test as the test image (Bugwood ID 5606064) — consecutive IDs from the same series! Let me view 2 more classes to complete the budget.
Bacterial_Canker shows internal brown canker lesions — no streaming, doesn't match. One more class needed.

This is the decisive evidence. The Bacterial_Wilt class has **multiple references** from the exact same Bugwood photo series showing the stem-in-beaker streaming test:
- Bugwood_11 (ID 5606059): Same beaker setup, stem in water
- Bugwood_3 (ID 5606063): Same beaker, white streaming visible
- **Test image (ID 5606064)**: Same beaker, white streaming — consecutive ID to Bugwood_3

All three are from the same sequential Bugwood series, all under Bacterial_Wilt. The Southern_Bacterial_Wilt references (e.g., Bugwood_13) show split stems with brown pith discoloration — a different type of image. The test image is clearly from the Bacterial_Wilt diagnostic series.
